requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: Executor installed createrepo_c, downloaded tree-1.8.0-10.el9.x86_64.rpm into /srv/local-repo while network was up, ran createrepo_c to generate repodata, and registered it as a file:// repo (/etc/yum.repos.d/local-file.repo). dnf --disablerepo=* --enablerepo=local-file repolist/list directly confirmed the local repo is readable and lists the package, and post-restart evidence confirms the repo storage and metadata remained intact.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repo while the usual remote repositories are unreachable
requirements.summary: All almalinux-*.repo files were disabled and iptables REJECT rules were added on tcp/80 and tcp/443. curl to mirrors.almalinux.org returned CONFIRMED-UNREACHABLE, directly demonstrating remote unreachability. dnf install -y --disablerepo=* --enablerepo=local-file tree then succeeded, and rpm -q tree / tree --version confirmed the package was installed solely from the local-file repo during this window.

requirements.requirement: Restore the environment to its normal state after simulating unreachability (remote repos re-enabled, firewall rules removed)
requirements.summary: iptables REJECT rules were deleted and verified absent, original repo files were restored with enabled=1, and curl confirmed remote reachability was restored. Post-restart evidence further confirms remote repos remained enabled/reachable and no leftover firewall rules existed.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (513c865e...) and healthy state (system running, tree installed, repo files intact) were captured. shutdown -r now was triggered in the background and returned an acknowledgement before disconnect; a following exec timed out (node down), and a subsequent poll succeeded with a new boot_id (bcd7d486...), matching the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check. Post-restart evidence confirmed the local repo storage/metadata, tree package, remote repo config, and firewall state all recovered correctly.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes of the task: it built and served a local file-based repository on node1, genuinely made the usual remote repos unreachable (repo files disabled plus iptables REJECT on 80/443, confirmed via curl), and successfully installed the tree package from the local repo during that window. It also restored the environment afterward and completed the mandatory node-restart protocol with direct pre/post boot-identity evidence and recovered state, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good with only minor leftover /tmp log files as residue.
limitations: Evaluation relies entirely on captured command outputs and fixed lifecycle snapshots; no live inspection was possible.
A handful of leftover /tmp log files from executor commands were not cleaned up, though this is low-risk residue not affecting task functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: installing repo tooling, building the local repo, temporarily disabling remote repos and blocking ports 80/443 (bounded and fully reverted in cmd-5a5c0777f6994ae9), installing the target package, and the mandatory reboot. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found, and the after_executor lifecycle comparison shows no failed services, no new listening sockets beyond the expected post-reboot restart of sshd/chronyd, and no package-health regressions. Minor residue: several /tmp log files (phaseA-install.log, phaseA-download.log, phaseA-createrepo.log, phaseB-install.log, clean.log, reboot.log) from the executor's own commands were left behind rather than cleaned up, a low-risk but avoidable residue.
